title: Cocartesian-arrow projection is a trivial Kan fibration onto its full vertex image
statement:
Use quasicategories, full simplicial subcategories, products, pullbacks and internal functor simplicial sets from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and trivial Kan fibrations from [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Work in a fixed containing universe. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories, and let $Y\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)$ be the full simplicial subset whose vertices are the $p$-cocartesian edges. Put
$$R=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}E,$$
where the map from $E$ to $B$ is $p$. The simplicial map $\theta:Y\to R$ sends an arrow $u$ to $(pu,u(0))$. Let $Z\subseteq R$ be the full simplicial subset spanned by those vertices $(\alpha,x)$ for which there exists a $p$-cocartesian edge with source $x$ and image $\alpha$. Then $\theta:Y\to Z$ is a trivial Kan fibration: it is surjective on vertices and lifts every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$, with exact agreement on the boundary and over $Z$. No existence of cocartesian lifts for vertices outside $Z$ is assumed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 5.2.1.3, opposite-category dual, including the full-image restriction Z and boundary lifting. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. This is a Kerodon identifier, not the unrelated Stacks tag.

proof.text: By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a simplex of $Y$ has all its vertices cocartesian arrows. Its image under $\theta$ therefore has all its vertices among the specified vertices of $Z$, so fullness makes $\theta$ factor through $Z$. Each vertex of $Z$ has a preimage by the defining existence condition on that vertex. This establishes precisely the dimension-zero condition of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], including when $Z$ is empty.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.1.3, definition of the full vertex image; source-endpoint dual.

proof.text: We first obtain the source-endpoint prism filtration from [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary]. Here are the order-reversal details, using the presheaf definition in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $\alpha:[a]\to[b]$, put $\rho(\alpha)(i)=b-\alpha(a-i)$. This is monotone, $\rho(\beta\alpha)=\rho(\beta)\rho(\alpha)$ and $\rho^2=1$. Set $(K^{\mathrm{op}})_a=K_a$ with operator $K(\rho(\alpha))$. This involutive operation preserves products, unions and pushout squares: it leaves their sets in every degree unchanged, and applying it twice recovers every map and every gluing problem. The isomorphism $(\Delta^r)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^r$ sends an $a$-simplex $f$ to $i\mapsto r-f(a-i)$. Thus it preserves boundaries, sends the horn indexed by $j$ to the horn indexed by $r-j$, and interchanges the two endpoints of $\Delta^1$. Apply it to the cited filtration for $m=n$. In the resulting prism the stage indexed by $q$ attaches the simplex $T_k$ for $k=n-q$, whose ordered vertices are $((0,0),\ldots,(0,k),(1,k),\ldots,(1,n))$, along $\Lambda_k^{n+1}$. The initial subcomplex is $A=(\{0\}\times\Delta^n)\cup(\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^n)$ and the attachment order is $k=n,n-1,\ldots,0$. The identification on prism vertices is $(\epsilon,i)\mapsto(1-\epsilon,n-i)$, and the horn index is $(n+1)-(q+1)=k$. These formulas follow directly from the standard simplices and products of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; no reversal map $[n]\to[n]$ is asserted to be monotone.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.1.3, prism filtration from Lemma 3.1.2.12 (Kerodon 00TH), with order-reversal dual spelled out.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$ and a lifting square $a:\partial\Delta^n\to Y$, $b:\Delta^n\to Z$ with $\theta a=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$. By the explicit internal functor simplicial set and degreewise pullback of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $b$ consists of $\bar h:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to B$ and $s:\Delta^n\to E$ with $ps=\bar h|_{\{0\}\times\Delta^n}$. The boundary datum gives $h_\partial:\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^n\to E$ over $\bar h$, with initial restriction $s|_{\partial\Delta^n}$. Glue $s$ and $h_\partial$ to $h_A:A\to E$. Their equality on the intersection makes this a degreewise well-defined map commuting with every simplicial operator. Every vertical edge over a vertex $i$ of $\Delta^n$ is already in $A$ and is $p$-cocartesian: for $n\geq1$ every vertex lies in the boundary, and $a$ takes values in $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.1.3, uncurrying the boundary lifting square, with endpoint 0 in the dual.

proof.text: Use the filtration established in Step 2. Inductively extend $h_A$ across the attachments $T_n,T_{n-1},\ldots,T_1$, requiring at every stage that its restriction to $A$ is exactly $h_A$ and that its composite with $p$ is exactly $\bar h$. The base stage is $h_A$. At attachment $T_k$, $1\leq k\leq n$, the existing map on its attaching horn and $\bar h|_{T_k}$ form a commutative lifting square for $\Lambda_k^{n+1}\subseteq\Delta^{n+1}$. Since $0<k<n+1$, the definition of inner fibration in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] supplies a filler. Glue that filler with the previously defined map along the attaching horn; the pushout from Step 2 gives the extended simplicial map. The two required equalities hold on both pieces and hence on their union. This proves the induction without altering any prescribed data.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.1.3, induction through the inner-horn attachments; dual order.

proof.text: The remaining attachment is $T_0$ along $\Lambda_0^{n+1}$. Its first two vertices are $(0,0),(1,0)$, so the distinguished edge $\{0,1\}$ is exactly the vertical edge at vertex 0 of the original prism. It lies in $A$, and its image is the $p$-cocartesian edge fixed in Step 3. As $n+1\geq2$, the cocartesian-edge definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] gives a filler of this last outer-horn lifting problem over $\bar h|_{T_0}$. Gluing along the horn as in Step 4 produces $h:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to E$ with $h|_A=h_A$ and $ph=\bar h$ exactly.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.1.3, last outer-horn attachment; cocartesian source-edge dual of the cartesian target-edge argument.

proof.text: Curry $h$ using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] to obtain $c:\Delta^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)$. Each vertex of $c$ is one of the vertical edges already fixed by $h_A$, hence is $p$-cocartesian; fullness therefore makes $c$ land in $Y$. Its boundary is $a$ because $h$ restricts to $h_\partial$, and $\theta c=b$ because $ph=\bar h$ and $h|_{\{0\}\times\Delta^n}=s$. This is equality in $Z$, since its inclusion into $R$ is degreewise injective. Together with Step 1, these fillers for every $n\geq1$ prove that $\theta:Y\to Z$ is a trivial Kan fibration in exactly the sense of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. The proof never requests a lift over a vertex outside $Z$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2.1.3, conclusion by currying and the full-subset condition, dualized.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 5.2.1.3, opposite-category dual; online source read, archival copy WANTED. The explicit order-reversal and boundary-preservation details are supplied here.

I checked by computer for n=1..5 that each T_k pulls the current stage back to exactly Lambda_k^{n+1} and that the stages cover the prism. Step 5: Lambda_0^{n+1} has the fixed cocartesian vertical edge at vertex 0 as its initial edge, and n+1>=2; I checked n=1 by hand. Step 6: currying lands in Y and gives the boundary a and theta c=b. proof_deps equals the union of the uses lists, and there is no cycle.
